reviews.one_line_contribution: It reframes the in-context-vs-weights cost comparison from the deployment horizon to the 'collection axis' and tests it with two matched scaling ladders on one pool and backbone — a bank-size ladder for retrieval and a pool-size ladder for QLoRA at matched optimizer steps — plus a procedure-held-out rotation, predicting that context saturates at ~3 items per task type (coverage-limited) while weights keep improving with item count (count-limited).
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified: 2608.15008 (Harness the Memory, 2026-08-15, verified via s2cli paper) is the closest substrate-comparison work; it evaluates dense/sparse indices, text records, structural and hierarchical stores, refinement memories, parametric updates and activation mechanisms in one harness and concludes no substrate dominates — but it reports regime-dependent trade-offs, not two matched scaling curves from one partitioned pool, so it does not pre-empt the ladder design. Verified: 2604.05533 (Echo, In-Context Analogy Learning, Minecraft, 2026-04-07) is the closest work on the cross-type half of E3; it adapts retrieved experiences to unseen tasks in context, with no weights arm, so it threatens P4's premise (analogy may transfer in context) rather than the design. Verified: 2607.21051 (Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience) matches RL baselines with >=9.6x fewer samples via Experience Distillation but has no matched-sample context arm. The sharpest threat to the proposal's premise is 2603.11076 (DIVE: Scaling Diversity in Agentic Task Synthesis for Generalizable Tool Use, 2026-03-10, verified via s2cli paper, 5 citations): diversity scaling outperforms quantity scaling for agentic SFT even with less data — i.e. the weights route has already been reported as coverage-limited rather than count-limited in a neighbouring setting, which is the opposite of P3 and is nowhere in the proposal's Related Work or collision check. Also relevant and missed: 2603.18272 (Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience, verified), which combines retrieval-augmented training with LoRA and reports improved generalization to unseen tasks — directly adjacent to E3's student-plus-cross-type-items arm.
reviews.strongest_objection: The two halves of the headline are, respectively, near-entailed and likely untestable. (a) P1/P2 are close to a restatement of what Measurement A already established plus the fact that ALFWorld has six task types: if the gain is procedure-bound and MiniLM retrieves on the goal sentence, then once the bank holds three same-type items the top-3 are same-type and the remaining ~420 near-duplicate items cannot add anything; P2 ('a bank missing a type loses that type's gain') is entailed by procedure-boundedness unless cross-type analogy works, which is exactly P4 — so the brief's own rule 'no prediction entailed by a definition' bites here. The proposal knows this (Risk 1) and relegates the only fix, the finer type x object x receptacle taxonomy, to an ablation. (b) The count-limited half rests on direct SFT as 'the main weights arm' while the proposal's own citation 2607.21051 reports direct SFT retaining 3.8% of the in-context gain; if rho(100%) < 0.4 the pre-registration declares P3 untestable (Gate 1), which also kills P5 and half of P4, leaving only the near-entailed context ladder. Context distillation, the arm most likely to clear Gate 1, is listed as 'an optional check'. (c) Even if both survive, the asymmetry is established by non-parallel manipulations: the context ladder varies coverage AND count (stratified vs type-blind), while the pool ladder is type-stratified at every size and therefore varies count at constant coverage — there is no coverage-poor weights condition, so 'context is coverage-limited, weights are count-limited' compares two different experiments; DIVE 2603.11076 makes this gap consequential, since it reports the coverage-poor manipulation being the one that hurts SFT. (d) The episode budget is understated by roughly 3x: E1's 25 bank configurations (4 sizes x 2 schemes x 3 subsample seeds, plus full B) x 494 tasks x 2 eval seeds is ~24,700 episodes for the k=3 arm alone, before decoys and the k=1 cells (~41,000 total), against a stated 16,400; E2's 8 students x 3 prompt conditions x 494 tasks x 3 eval seeds is ~35,600 against a stated 11,900. 'About three days' on two A100s, one of which is training, is not credible at ~90,000 episodes. (e) The 'collection axis' is vacuous on the expert pool: ALFWorld walkthroughs ship with the benchmark and cost nothing to collect, so the only arm where x actually measures collection cost is the own-rollout replication E5, which is contingent on a pool that 'may be incomplete in time' (Risk 6).
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes. (1) Make context distillation with its P-CD0 control the primary weights arm and direct SFT the secondary, so Gate 1 has a realistic chance of passing and P3/P5 are actually resolvable; state the expected rho per objective from 2607.21051 up front. (2) Test the asymmetry with the same manipulation on both substrates: add a type-blind / coverage-poor training pool ladder (a count-matched pool drawn from two types, and a one-item-per-type pool) alongside the stratified pool ladder, making it a 2x2 of substrate x manipulation, and engage DIVE 2603.11076 directly as the prior that predicts the opposite of P3. (3) Promote the finer taxonomy (type x object x receptacle) to the primary definition of coverage so P1's saturation point is not fixed by the six-type template, and add the static no-retrieval baseline that P1's own success implies. (4) Move the own-rollout pool from contingent E5 into the confirmatory design, since it is the only pool on which the collection axis has a measured cost, and label the expert-pool frontier as hypothetical cost accounting. Also re-derive the episode budget cell by cell and cut seeds or splits explicitly rather than reporting a total the design does not produce.
reviews.missing_baseline: A static, no-retrieval procedure prompt: 1 or 3 hand-picked exemplars per task type concatenated into every prompt, with no retriever and no bank. If P1 is true — 18 items recover >=80% of the full-bank gain — then retrieval buys nothing over a fixed 18-example prefix, and the honest substrate comparison becomes 'static few-shot prompt vs weights', not 'retrieval vs weights'. Without this arm the paper cannot say whether it measured coverage saturation or simply that a retriever is unnecessary on a six-template benchmark, and a reviewer will demand it because it is the cheapest arm in the entire plan. Secondary omission: a coverage-poor (type-blind) training pool for the weights ladder, without which P3's 'count-limited' label is never contrasted against the same alternative the context arm is contrasted against.
reviews.preprint_collision: No VERIFIED COLLISION found. All six of my queries were answered by channel (a), the literature command (S2 + HF); WebSearch was unavailable this session and WebFetch was never used. Queries and returns: (1) 'retrieval bank size scaling versus fine-tuning pool size agent experience memory substrate' --recent -> 2608.15008, 2607.26637, 2607.00394, 2606.24775, 2606.06448, 2605.12493, 2604.03295, 2509.25140 — memory-system profiling and substrate benchmarking, no matched bank/pool ladders. (2) 'how many demonstrations per task type are needed retrieval saturates coverage in-context agent ALFWorld' --recent -> 2608.15930, 2608.14943, 2604.24594, 2505.00234 plus unrelated benchmarks — nothing on demonstration-count saturation per procedure. (3) 'in-context learning versus fine-tuning cost crossover number of examples break-even compute' --recent -> only 2506.11103, 2506.04579, 2503.09032 (many-shot ICL and gradient-matching demonstration selection); nothing agentic. (4) 'task diversity versus data quantity scaling supervised fine-tuning agent trajectories coverage' --recent -> 2603.11076 DIVE (diversity scaling beats quantity scaling for agentic tool-use SFT), 2608.02287, 2607.19523, 2602.07153 — DIVE is not a collision (no context arm, no ALFWorld, no cost frontier) but it is a cited, id-verified prior result pointing the opposite way from P3, and the proposal's check missed the whole diversity-vs-quantity SFT scaling literature. (5) 'fine-tuned agent generalizes to held-out task type while retrieved demonstrations do not' -> 2603.18272 (retrieval-augmented training + LoRA improves unseen-task generalization), 2604.27003, 2501.17161, 2501.01702 — 2603.18272 is adjacent to E3 and also missing from the proposal's check. (6) 'memory bank size ablation saturation number of stored experiences diminishing returns' --recent -> 2608.06811, 2607.10608, 2606.24595, 2603.04549, 2602.19320 — admission control and memory-consumption diagnostics, no size ladder. ID verification via s2cli paper: 2604.05533 (Echo) VERIFIED, 2607.21051 VERIFIED, 2608.15008 VERIFIED, 2603.18272 VERIFIED, 2603.11076 (DIVE) VERIFIED. I did not verify 2607.26017 (UniMem), 2608.01234 (COVE), 2604.02268 (SKILL0), 2606.02355 (SIRI), 2512.02543 or 2507.06219, which the Related Work leans on. Judgement of the proposal's own check: above average for this round — four queries, IDs attached, the WebSearch gap disclosed, empty returns reported as empty rather than as proof of novelty. Its weakness is scope, not honesty: every query aims at the agent-memory/substrate literature and none at the two scaling literatures the claim actually inhabits (many-shot ICL demonstration-count scaling, and SFT diversity-vs-quantity scaling), which is how DIVE and 2603.18272 were missed. The un-scooped part of this proposal is the design — two ladders on one backbone with a procedure-held-out boundary — not the hypothesis, and I score novelty accordingly.
